fraudIntel.title: Fraud risk overview
fraudIntel.subtitle: Operational context from Shopify's fraud analysis — never a fraud-prevention decision tool.
fraudIntel.queuedBody: We've queued up an analysis of your historical orders. This usually starts within a few minutes — refresh in a bit to see progress.
fraudIntel.analyzingBody: We've analyzed {count} orders so far. The risk overview unlocks the moment we finish.
fraudIntel.failedTitle: We hit a snag analyzing your orders
fraudIntel.failedBody: Our background job didn't complete. We'll retry automatically — refresh in a few minutes.
fraudIntel.tooltipAcceptanceRate: Share of analyzed orders that Shopify cleared or rated low/medium risk. Orders still pending fraud analysis are excluded; orders Shopify marked as having no risk indicators are counted as accepted.
fraudIntel.tooltipHighRiskRate: Share of orders Shopify classified as HIGH risk during fraud analysis.
fraudIntel.tooltipFraudDisputeRate: Share of orders that became a Shopify Payments fraud dispute (reason = FRAUDULENT) in this window.
fraudIntel.tooltipHighRiskFulfilled: Of orders classified HIGH risk, the share that still reached a fulfilled state. A high number can signal operational exposure.
fraudIntel.tooltipProtectCoverage: Of order value Shopify Protect was eligible to underwrite, the share marked PROTECTED.
fraudIntel.tooltipOrdersAnalyzed: Total Shopify orders covered by this window. Backfill anchors to the historical scope granted to the app.
fraudIntel.bannerBody: {high}% of recent orders were classified as high-risk by Shopify's fraud analysis. {fulfilled}% of Shopify high-risk orders were still fulfilled. You can now monitor fraud-risk exposure, operational patterns, and dispute trends directly inside DisputeDesk.
fraudIntel.bannerHealthInsufficient: Building baseline — too few recent orders to surface a meaningful rate yet.
fraudIntel.chargebackHealthInsufficientBody: We've observed {count} orders in the last 90 days — not enough to classify chargeback health into a meaningful band. The verdict surfaces automatically once volume increases.
fraudIntel.pageSubtitle: Operational context from Shopify's fraud signals — not a fraud-prevention decision.
fraudIntel.pageBody: {high}% of recent orders were classified as high-risk by Shopify's fraud analysis. {fulfilled}% of those high-risk orders were still fulfilled. Use this view to monitor exposure, operational patterns, and dispute trends.
fraudIntel.pageScopeNoteDefault: Your store granted the default order-history scope, so this analysis covers the trailing 60 days. The window expands automatically once Shopify approves extended history access.
fraudIntel.chargebackHealthExplain: Calculated from your trailing 90-day chargeback rate. Industry monitoring thresholds align with card-network programs.
fraudIntel.whatThisMeansBody: Fraud-risk classification is one operational signal among many. DisputeDesk treats it as context for dispute correlation and merchant operations — never as a verdict on individual orders.
fraudIntel.stripBody: We've analyzed {count} historical Shopify orders. {high}% were classified high-risk by Shopify's fraud analysis. {fulfilled}% of those high-risk orders were still fulfilled.
fraudIntel.stripPreparingBody: Preparing operational insights — your historical analysis is still in progress. The summary lands here once it finishes.
fraudIntel.breakdownExplainBannerTitle: Cleared vs Low — what's the difference?
fraudIntel.breakdownExplainBannerBody: Low means Shopify found explicit POSITIVE signals (returning customer, billing/shipping match, established email domain). Cleared means Shopify analyzed the order but found no strong signals in either direction — no red flags AND no positive endorsements. Both are safe to accept; Low just has more positive evidence behind it. On a healthy store the majority of orders end up in Cleared simply because most customers don't trigger anything noteworthy.
fraudIntel.breakdownExplainHigh: Shopify detected multiple NEGATIVE signals (e.g. VPN use, parcel-forwarder address, billing/shipping mismatch in a high-fraud region). Recommended for manual review.
fraudIntel.breakdownExplainMedium: A few concerning or ambiguous signals worth a second look (e.g. first-time customer, order placed outside the store's typical hours).
fraudIntel.breakdownExplainLow: Shopify found explicit POSITIVE signals — returning customer with successful prior orders, billing/shipping match, established email domain. High confidence the order is legitimate.
fraudIntel.breakdownExplainPending: Shopify hasn't finished its fraud check on this order yet — a verdict appears later.
fraudIntel.breakdownExplainCleared: Shopify completed its analysis but didn't find strong signals in either direction — no red flags AND no explicit positive indicators. Different from Low: Low means "I see reasons to trust this"; Cleared means "I see no reason to flag this." Most orders end up here on a healthy store.
fraudIntel.correlationSubtitle: How often each Shopify risk level on your store has converted to an actual dispute. Observed, not predicted.
fraudIntel.correlationObservationStrong: On your store, orders Shopify classified as high-risk became disputes about {ratio}x more often than orders Shopify cleared or rated low-risk. This is a strong observed correlation — high-risk orders are worth manual review.
fraudIntel.correlationObservationMild: On your store, orders Shopify classified as high-risk became disputes about {ratio}x more often than orders Shopify cleared or rated low-risk. The signal is mild, not overwhelming.
fraudIntel.correlationObservationFlat: On your store, high-risk and low-risk orders have converted to disputes at similar rates so far. Shopify's classification has not provided strong predictive separation for your dataset yet.
fraudIntel.correlationObservationInverted: Unusual — on your store, high-risk orders have converted to disputes at a similar or lower rate than orders Shopify cleared. This can happen when the dispute sample is small or when disputes are driven by post-purchase issues (delivery, product) rather than fraud signals.
fraudIntel.correlationObservationNeedHigh: Not enough high-risk orders observed yet to compute a meaningful correlation. Conversion ratios will appear here once volume builds.
fraudIntel.correlationObservationNeedSafe: Not enough low-risk or cleared orders observed yet to compute a meaningful correlation baseline.

fraudIntel.scopeUpgradeBody: DisputeDesk now supports analyzing your full historical orders, not just the last 60 days. Re-authorize to expand the risk overview with seasonality, long-window trends, and risk-to-dispute correlation.
fraudIntel.kpiAcceptanceRateInfo: Share of analyzed orders Shopify accepted at checkout — meaning the fraud analysis did not block them. Excludes orders still pending fraud analysis.
fraudIntel.kpiHighRiskRateInfo: Share of orders Shopify classified as HIGH risk during fraud analysis. A higher number signals more exposure to chargebacks.
fraudIntel.kpiFraudDisputeRateInfo: Share of orders that became a Shopify Payments fraud dispute (reason = FRAUDULENT) in this window.
fraudIntel.kpi3dsAuthInfo: Share of Shopify Payments card orders where 3-D Secure authentication completed successfully. Authenticated payments shift liability to the issuer for fraud chargebacks.
fraudIntel.kpiProtectCoverageInfo: Of orders Shopify Protect was eligible to underwrite, the share marked PROTECTED. Protected orders do not reach you as chargebacks.
fraudIntel.kpiMedianFulfillmentInfo: Median time between order placement and fulfillment, across orders fulfilled in this window. Faster fulfillment generally improves customer-service signals.
fraudIntel.kpiHighRiskFulfilledInfo: Of orders Shopify classified HIGH risk, the share that still reached a fulfilled state. A high number means you are absorbing the fraud risk Shopify flagged.
fraudIntel.kpiConfirmedDeliveryInfo: Of fulfilled orders, the share where the carrier returned a delivered status. Carrier-attested delivery is strong dispute evidence.
fraudIntel.kpiSignedForInfo: Of confirmed deliveries, the share where the carrier recorded a signature. Signature confirmation is the strongest delivery evidence for fraud chargebacks.
fraudIntel.checkpointsSubtitle: Where you stand relative to card-network rules and your own 30-day baseline.
fraudIntel.checkpoint_chargeback_rate_vs_vamp_healt: Your 90-day chargeback rate is {current}. Visa's VAMP Excessive threshold is {vampExcessive}; the operationally watched 'approaching' band begins around {vampApproaching}.
fraudIntel.checkpoint_chargeback_rate_vs_vamp_consi: Your 90-day chargeback rate is {current} — inside the {vampApproaching}–{vampExcessive} 'approaching' band. Acquirers face $8 per disputed transaction once Excessive ({vampExcessive}) is reached.
fraudIntel.checkpoint_chargeback_rate_vs_vamp_breac: Your 90-day chargeback rate is {current}, at or above Visa's VAMP Excessive threshold of {vampExcessive}. Acquirers face $8 per disputed transaction at this level.
fraudIntel.checkpoint_chargeback_rate_vs_ecm_health: Your 90-day chargeback rate is {current}, well below Mastercard's ECM ratio of {ecmRatio} (which also requires {ecmCount}+ chargebacks per month).
fraudIntel.checkpoint_chargeback_rate_vs_ecm_consid: Your 90-day chargeback rate is {current}. Mastercard's ECM activates at {ecmRatio} ratio with {ecmCount}+ chargebacks per month (you average ~{monthlyEstimate}).
fraudIntel.checkpoint_chargeback_rate_vs_ecm_breach: Your 90-day chargeback rate is {current} and you average ~{monthlyEstimate} chargebacks per month. Both ECM criteria ({ecmRatio} ratio, {ecmCount}+/month) are now met.
fraudIntel.checkpoint_high_risk_fulfilled_consider_: Each fulfilled HIGH-risk order is absorbed exposure — Shopify's risk model flagged but did not block. Set up a Shopify Flow rule that holds fulfillment when an order is High-risk and over a value threshold you choose.
fraudIntel.checkpoint_signature_capture_low_conside: Signature captured on {current} of confirmed deliveries.
Carrier-attested signature confirmation is the strongest delivery evidence in fraud-coded chargebacks. Requiring signature on higher-value shipments meaningfully strengthens dispute defense.
fraudIntel.checkpoint_threeds_auth_healthy_title: 3-DS authentication on {current} of eligible card orders.
fraudIntel.checkpoint_threeds_auth_healthy_body: Authenticated payments shift fraud-chargeback liability to the issuer under Visa's liability-shift rules. Coverage at this level is operationally strong.
fraudIntel.checkpoint_threeds_auth_info_title: 3-DS authentication on {current} of eligible card orders.
fraudIntel.checkpoint_threeds_auth_info_body: Visa's liability shift moves fraud-chargeback responsibility to the issuer for authenticated payments. Coverage above 25% is the operationally strong band.
fraudIntel.checkpoint_threeds_auth_consider_title: 3-DS authentication on {current} of eligible card orders.
fraudIntel.checkpoint_threeds_auth_consider_body: Authenticated payments shift fraud-chargeback liability to the issuer. Coverage this low leaves most card-not-present fraud disputes recoverable only through evidence packs.
fraudIntel.checkpoint_protect_coverage_low_info_bod: Underwritten orders do not reach you as chargebacks. Lower coverage means a larger share of disputes are yours to defend with evidence packs.
fraudIntel.checkpoint_fulfillment_baseline_degraded: Up {delta} versus prior 30 days ({prior}). Faster fulfillment generally strengthens customer-service signals — and is a routinely cited dispute factor.
fraudIntel.checkpoint_fulfillment_baseline_improved: Down {delta} versus prior 30 days ({prior}). Faster fulfillment strengthens customer-service signals in non-fraud disputes.
